prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-24, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-24):
| Current ratio           | 0.53 |
| Retained earnings       | -12,237M |
| Current liabilities     | 6,106M |
| Current assets          | 3,244M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 12,807M |
| Total liabilities       | 43,578M |
| Total assets            | 58,573M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,307M |
| Revenue                 | 3,198M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows stretched liquidity (current ratio 0.53) and high leverage (total liabilities to assets ~74%), with negative retained earnings, indicating weakened financial flexibility despite a seemingly solid EBIT relative to revenue. Overall credit risk appears to be below investment-grade but not severely distressed, aligning with a BBB- assessment.

DECISION: BBB-
